thesis: A model is an explicit typed computational structure assembled from composable primitives; named architectures are reference constructions, not the repository ontology.
owns: recurrent regions and iterative depth structure
routers gates sparse activation and conditional computation structure
structural model identity and topology digests
core_invariants: composition is preferred over named architecture silos
model structure is explicit and inspectable
structure is distinguishable from learned parameter and state artifacts
recurrence is first class and is not defined only by unrolling
routing and sparse conditional computation are first class
heterogeneous submodels may compose through typed interfaces
model components are addressable by stable identities
execution placement is separate from model semantics
learning is performed through mncs-learn rather than duplicated here
storage is performed through mncs-store or the appropriate owner rather than duplicated here
memory interfaces do not transfer ownership of memory semantics into this repository
bootstrap host artifacts are not permanent normative authority
the repository maintains one evolving canonical implementation unless a real external compatibility requirement exists

family_interfaces.mncs-language: native model representation and generic executable semantics
family_interfaces.MNCS-Commons: shared identities types and cross-family contracts where appropriate
family_interfaces.mncs-learn: evidence-governed mutation of addressable model state routing relationships and topology
family_interfaces.mncs-ingest: typed observations and data presented to model interfaces
family_interfaces.mncs-memory: memory behavior retrieval and persistent memory semantics exposed through explicit model interfaces
family_interfaces.mncs-store: durable model parameter state checkpoint and artifact persistence
family_interfaces.mncs-rights-provenance: rights provenance and lineage constraints for construction sources and model artifacts
family_interfaces.mncs-fabric: worker device and distributed execution placement
family_interfaces.mncs-debug: diagnosis of model construction and execution failures

research_policy.default: express new architectures using existing primitives before adding new ontology
research_policy.new_primitive_requirement: identify the smallest general missing semantic capability and justify it beyond one paper-specific implementation
research_policy.reference_architectures: known architecture families are reproducible constructions over common primitives
tracked_families: autoregressive diffusion flow energy-based and other generative models

evolution_policy: Maintain one canonical implementation and migrate known MNCS consumers forward. Do not create frozen v1/v2/legacy/next implementation trees without a real compatibility obligation.
